witness.n_range: 0 <= n <= p + ceil(p^c) inclusive, per (p, c)
witness.property: for each (p, c, n): exists integers a, b with n < a < n + p^c, n < b < n + p^c (STRICT real bound: allowed integers n+1 .. n+floor(p^c), minus the endpoint when p^c is an exact integer) and (a*b) mod p == 1
witness.note: Fragment narrowed relative to L1's recorded scope: prime p=3 is EXCLUDED because (p,c,n)=(3,3/5,2) is a genuine counterexample — the strict interval (2, 2+3^(3/5)) contains only the integer 3, and 3*3 ≡ 0 mod 3. All other primes in range are retained.
witness.expected: verify(witness) returns True; raises on any counterexample

claim: Exact fail-closed integer verification (exact arithmetic, no floats, no I/O, strict real-bound interval handling via exact integer floor/ceil roots) that for every prime 5<=p<=43, every c in {3/5,3/4,1,3/2}, and every 0<=n<=p+ceil(p^c), there exist a,b in the strict interval (n, n+p^c) with ab≡1 mod p. This certifies the finite enumerated scope of L1 restricted to primes >= 5; the prime 3 case is refuted (see witness.note) and general-p scaling remains analytic.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
